Code: reattemptOf runs in section 7b, after every status rule. A contract is a re-attempt when origin.parentId, or the leading id parsed from origin.parent (/^([A-Z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*)\b/), names a register item whose status is not PASS or CLOSED_PASS. toSelectorCandidates then maps it to the non-selectable status REATTEMPT_WITHOUT_CHANGED_INPUT. This happens only when no non-empty preRegistration.changedInput or origin.changedInput is given, and never to CLOSED_* items. The new status is added to the selector's EXPLAINED_DEFAULTS.
The parse is sound for the 'ID (…)' convention: 'V178-P1 (CLOSED_FAIL …)' parses to V178-P1, and 'V178-P4 (CLOSED_PASS …)' is correctly not a re-attempt.

The parse is not fail-safe, but it only adds a restriction and weakens no existing guard. An unparseable parent or one absent from the register yields 'not a re-attempt' (fail-open to the prior behaviour). V19-EXP-B ('EXPERIENCE …' parses to EXPERIENCE) and V19-MEM-2 (parent V19-MEM-1, not a register item) are silently skipped.

Scope limit the validation must state: detection relies on a declared origin.parent or parentId. G2 and J2, the very cases behind the original OL-8 finding, have no origin.parent, so this rule would not have caught them.

Further limits. 'changedInput' is accepted as any non-empty string or object: the gate checks that a changed input is CITED, not MEASURED, although the objective says 'measured'. A parent that is NOT_STARTED also triggers the rule, which is over-blocking but fail-closed.
On the real register, only V178-P1-R is detected (parent V178-P1 CLOSED_FAIL), and it is CLOSED_FAIL itself, so selection is unaffected.

AC1 and AC2 are tested on synthetic fixtures through the real toSelectorCandidates and selectNextExplained. With no changed input, the status becomes REATTEMPT_WITHOUT_CHANGED_INPUT and the item is not selected. With a cited input, the status stays NOT_STARTED. A third check covers a PASS parent and the no-parent case. The tests prove the claims as written.
